name: Meshach
title: One of Daniel's three friends in Babylon
summary: Meshach was one of the three young Jewish men taken into captivity to Babylon along with Daniel. He received the Babylonian name Meshach. He is best known for refusing to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden image and for being thrown into the blazing furnace, from which he was miraculously saved by God.

keyEvents.title: Taken to Babylon
keyEvents.description: Meshach was among the young Jewish men of royal descent who were chosen to serve at Nebuchadnezzar's court in Babylon.

keyEvents.title: Received the Babylonian name Meshach
keyEvents.description: The chief official gave Meshach the Babylonian name Meshach as part of the process of assimilating the Jewish captives into Babylonian culture.

keyEvents.title: Refused to eat the king's food
keyEvents.description: Along with Daniel, Hananiah and Azariah, Meshach refused to defile himself with the king's food and drink, choosing instead to eat vegetables and drink water.

keyEvents.title: Appointed to govern the province of Babylon
keyEvents.description: After Daniel interpreted Nebuchadnezzar's dream, he asked the king to appoint Mishael, Hananiah, and Azariah to administer the province of Babylon.

keyEvents.title: Refused to worship the golden image
keyEvents.description: Mishael, along with Hananiah and Azariah, refused to bow down before Nebuchadnezzar's great golden image and was accused of disobedience to the king's command.

keyEvents.title: Saved from the blazing furnace
keyEvents.description: The three men were thrown into a blazing furnace, but God sent an angel to protect them. They came out of the fire unharmed, with not even their hair singed or their clothes smelling of smoke. Nebuchadnezzar praised God after this miracle.
